html:
The Penobscot are an Indigenous people of the Penobscot River valley in what is now Maine. They are one of the nations of the Wabanaki Confederacy, with the Passamaquoddy, the Maliseet, the Mi'kmaq and the Abenaki.

They moved with the seasons: inland to hunt in winter, to the coast in summer for fish and shellfish, travelling by birchbark canoe. In the 1600s and 1700s they traded with and fought beside New France against the English colonists. Their main village today is on Indian Island in the river at Old Town.

In 1980 the Maine Indian Claims Settlement Act settled their land claims with money to buy back land. In the 2010s two dams on the river were removed to let sea run fish return, a project the Penobscot helped lead.
